request.spec:
Clients who ignore my reminders shouldn't get more credit. While a client has an invoice that
is still overdue after its final notice (the third reminder) went out, put them on hold
automatically, with everything a hold means; and while they have one still overdue after its
second reminder, make every one of their drafts need approval.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for this implementation's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Clients who ignore my reminders shouldn't get more credit. While a client has an invoice that
is still overdue after its final notice (the third reminder) went out, put them on hold
automatically, with everything a hold means; and while they have one still overdue after its
second reminder, make every one of their drafts need approval.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've made the change and `bin/e2e` passes, including the replay of earlier tests' data.

**What the app does now** (all server-side; the screens already show whatever the server reports):
- **Automatic hold:** a client goes on hold while any of their sent invoices is still overdue after its third reminder (the final notice) went out. The hold lifts once that invoice is paid. It is a full hold: their invoices can't be sent, credit can't be applied, the client shows "On hold", and a payment goes to their overdue invoices first. The "Lift hold" button refuses while the final notice is unpaid, and says why. This works the same way as the existing automatic hold for disputes open more than 30 days.
- **Approval:** while any of a client's invoices is still overdue after its second reminder, every one of their drafts needs approval. Trying to send one without approval gives an error naming the unpaid second reminder as the reason.
- "Still overdue" uses the app's usual overdue status, so an invoice covered by an active promise to pay doesn't trigger either rule.

**One behaviour change you should know about:** the test records the payment from the payment form on Acme's draft invoice. Until now the server always refused payments against a draft. For a client on hold it now accepts the payment and puts it toward their overdue invoices first, which is what the existing comment on the on-hold payment code already described. For clients not on hold, drafts are still refused.

The changes are in `InvoiceService.java`, `Invoice.java` (`approval` takes one more flag) and `ClientController.java`.
